item.text:
**1B.3 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

Overall read: **slightly positive but low confidence**. The best 2024 evidence is administrative and declaratory: Bangladesh’s leadership publicly emphasized safety/security, IAEA support, and spent-fuel return planning. I did **not** find a 2024 report of a specific nuclear safety breakdown, but I also did **not** find strong 2024 proof of major new command-and-control tightening beyond official assurances.

**Accepted claims**

- **Consider setting up 2nd nuclear power plant**
  - **Publisher:** The Daily Star / UNB
  - **Date:** April 2, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/consider-setting-2nd-nuclear-power-plant-3580751](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/consider-setting-2nd-nuclear-power-plant-3580751)
  - **Claim-level summary:** Hasina asked Rosatom to consider a second Rooppur plant and directed the authorities to complete formalities for taking back spent nuclear fuel from the first and second units to Russia. That is the clearest 2024 evidence of custody / back-end risk management I found.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.3, 1B.1

- **Bangladesh reaffirms commitment to nuclear non-proliferation, peaceful use**
  - **Publisher:** Dhaka Tribune
  - **Date:** April 30, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/foreign-affairs/345281/bangladesh-reaffirms-commitment-to-nuclear](https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/foreign-affairs/345281/bangladesh-reaffirms-commitment-to-nuclear)
  - **Claim-level summary:** The foreign minister said Bangladesh would maintain the highest level of transparency, safety, and security for its nuclear power plants and highlighted IAEA support for training and capacity building on safety and safeguards. This is strong positive evidence for discipline and accident-prevention intent.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.3, 1B.2

- **Bangladesh puts energy hopes in first nuclear power plant, despite delay**
  - **Publisher:** Thomson Reuters Foundation, republished by Prothom Alo
  - **Date:** January 6, 2023
  - **URL:** [https://en.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/bangladesh-in-world-media/js08b2eas8](https://en.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/bangladesh-in-world-media/js08b2eas8)
  - **Claim-level summary:** Experts quoted in the piece questioned affordability and safety, said Bangladesh’s capacity to manage a large nuclear disaster was limited, and noted missing public information on climate-related design risk. This is negative context, but it is background rather than 2024-specific evidence.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.3

**Synthesis**

- The 2024 record contains **some affirmative safety/custody signals**:
  - spent-fuel return planning,
  - public commitment to transparency and high safety/security,
  - IAEA-backed training and safeguards language.
- The **best negative material** I found is **background criticism**, not a 2024 incident:
  - dependence on Russian technology,
  - expert doubts about disaster-response capacity,
  - uncertainty about climate-risk integration.
- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Hasina personally weakened nuclear command-and-control discipline or that a nuclear accident/security failure occurred.
- I also found **no strong 2024 evidence** of a major new institutional strengthening beyond the existing official safeguards posture.

**Search gap**

- I searched directly for 2024 Rooppur safety, safeguards, command-and-control, accident prevention, and nuclear security formulations.
- The result set was thin on **direct ruler-level operational evidence**.
- The available evidence is mostly **policy declarations and project-level safeguards language**, not audited evidence of implementation quality.
